title: Why Investors Stop Checking Accounts When Markets Drop
alt_title_1: The Ostrich Effect: How Avoiding Bad Financial News Costs You
alt_title_2: What Vanguard Login Data Revealed About Investor Psychology
description_hook: In 2009, economists Niklas Karlsson, George Loewenstein, and Duane Seppi analyzed investor login patterns in the Journal of Risk and Uncertainty and proved the Ostrich Effect. Here is when ignoring financial data helps and when it quietly hurts.

scenes.headline: Why Portfolio Logins Vanish During Red Weeks
bullets: Green market weeks trigger constant account refreshes
Red weeks make people avoid opening financial apps
scenes.narration: Notice how eagerly people check their brokerage app during a bull run, then stop opening the app the week markets drop?
scenes.source: Karlsson, Loewenstein & Seppi, Journal of Risk and Uncertainty (2009)

scenes.headline: Karlsson, Loewenstein & Seppi's Login Study
bullets: Investors monitored portfolios heavily after market gains
Logins dropped sharply whenever indexes fell or stalled
scenes.narration: In 2009, economists Niklas Karlsson, George Loewenstein, and Duane Seppi analyzed Vanguard and Scandinavian pension logins in the Journal of Risk and Uncertainty. Account checks surged on up days and fell sharply during downturns.
scenes.source: Karlsson, Loewenstein & Seppi, 'The Ostrich Effect', JRU (2009)

scenes.headline: Healthy Market Calm vs Costly Bill Avoidance
scenes.left_body: Ignoring card balances, taxes & leaks -> penalties multiply
scenes.right_body: Automated index buys + calm weekly cashflow check -> full control
scenes.narration: They called this selective attention the Ostrich Effect. Ignoring daily stock noise helps long-term holders, yet avoiding credit statements, tax bills, and cash leaks lets penalties quietly multiply.

scenes.headline: Automate Long-Term Assets, Audit Weekly Cash
scenes.stat_subtext: Zero emotional market timing + 100% visibility on monthly bills
scenes.narration: Separate volatile investments from monthly cashflow: automate index contributions so market dips need zero monitoring, while auditing bills on a fixed weekly calendar.

scenes.headline: The 15-Minute Friday Financial Check-In
scenes.stat_label: REPLACE MOOD-BASED CHECKS WITH A RITUAL
bullets: Review checking, upcoming bills, and subscriptions every Friday
Facts on a spreadsheet shrink anxiety faster than avoidance
scenes.narration: Run a calm fifteen-minute Friday money check regardless of mood so bad news never compounds in the dark.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule of thumb (advice, not a study)
